prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Database column specification for orders table (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Column" · longest unbreakable word 137px · one-line width 137px
  col 2: header "Type" · longest unbreakable word 99px · one-line width 210px
  col 3: header "Nullable" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 59px
  col 4: header "Default" · longest unbreakable word 161px · one-line width 161px
  col 5: header "Comment" · longest unbreakable word 93px · one-line width 577px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Document the orders table schema, including each column’s data type, nullability, default and meaning.","reading":"Readers locate a column by name, scan across its row for its specification, and compare types, nullability and defaults down their respective columns. Wrapped comments and types can share the same row height.","groups":["Column and Type identify each field and its stored representation.","Nullable and Default describe behavior when a value is absent.","Comment explains the field in prose and supports interpretation of the specification."],"keep_intact":["Column identifiers such as total_amount_cents","Individual type tokens such as VARCHAR(32) and TIMESTAMP","Default expressions and literals such as CURRENT_TIMESTAMP and 'pending'","NO and YES"],"may_wrap":["Comments at spaces between words","Multiword types such as TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE and BIGINT UNSIGNED at spaces"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [158, 120, 80, 182, 179] · table 720×885px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [158, 130, 80, 182, 169] · table 720×955px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 129, 106, 106, 106, 129, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [158, 119, 80, 182, 180] · table 720×885px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 2

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
